journey.title: 1  Hopper
journey.text: Thirty balls (Ø22.7, 1.83 g) wait in the clear hopper. Gravity drops them into the dial's pockets; the cone on top of the dial stirs the pile so they cannot bridge.

journey.title: 2  Feed dial
journey.text: A servo under the dial (the same STS3215 as pan and tilt) steps it 45 deg per ball in about 235 ms: 3 balls/s, 3 at most. It reads its own load, so it feels a jam and backs off. Parked, a spoke sits over the exit hole, so no ball can reach the wheels, powered or not.

journey.title: 3  Exit hole
journey.text: At the front of the housing (37 mm ahead of the dial axis) a pocket passes over a hole in the floor and its ball drops out. About 235 ms from the command (the servo's step).

journey.title: 4  Chute
journey.text: A quarter bend of radius 21.4 mm turns the falling ball forward onto the path, 15 mm under the tilt axis. It takes about 86 ms and reaches the wheels at 0.65 m/s.

journey.title: 5  Flywheels
journey.text: Two Ø38 wheels 52 mm apart spin opposite ways at about 15,290 rpm (97 % of the X2216's no-load speed on its trimmed rail). The gap is 9.08 mm narrower than the ball (40.0 % squeeze), so it leaves at the tyres' surface speed. Each wheel stores 9.53 J; a shot costs about 2.6 % of its speed, back in 4.6 ms at a 10 A current limit.

journey.title: 6  Barrel
journey.text: 100 mm long, bore Ø24.7: 2 mm over the ball, so it only guides. Two IR gates 60 mm apart time every ball (a built-in chronograph); 4.3 ms from the nip to the muzzle.

journey.title: 7  Muzzle
journey.text: 28.96 m/s (95.0 fps set; the physical ceiling is 105), 0.767 J. The barrel can never point above level: hard stops at 0 and -25 deg in the yoke. About 337 ms from the command to here.

journey.title: 8  Flight
journey.text: Air drag and gravity: a level shot from the bench has dropped 112 mm at 3 m and slowed to 17.5 m/s. The laser is parallel to the barrel, so at range the ball lands under the dot.

flywheel.note: the set speed for the nominal ball at the physics' set fps (sim/turret_launch3d.py); foam loss 30 % (assumed); the chronograph gates in the barrel measure the real speed

flight_level.note: a level shot from the bench (the box on a 0.3 m crate): [range m, time s, drop mm, speed m/s]; drag as a sphere, Cd 0.5

clearance.note: antennas: upright swivel dipoles on all four RP-SMA bulkheads (none chosen yet: typical 2.4 GHz swivel dipole, Ø10 x 108 (est; none chosen))

ball_path.note: every pan and tilt clear of the deck, the box and upright antennas by the margin; no firing within 60 deg of straight back (the operator's side)

fan.note: 9215-Y at full speed (12 V, 4000 rpm): 55.26 CFM free air, 2.87 mmH2O at zero flow (S06 p.2); straight-line curve between the two. Blows up: it pulls air in through the fin block's open sides and out through the lid grille (user, 2026-10-27, on the fitted cooler).

operating_point.note: the J501's CFD of the bare box at 40 W in 25 C air

airflow.method: losses K x 0.5 rho v^2 (rho 1.2): K = 1 through the grille's gaps (the entry and the bars), K = 1 for the turn down into the fan on the whole flow across the duct over the fan's centre; the box's own resistance as k q^2 through the J501 CFD's operating point; the fan's straight-line curve from its J501 parameters (dp0, q_free); the new flow where the two meet
airflow.not_modelled: the open roof cells the shroud's floor covers (they vent through the 1 mm under it: intake_seal; bounded in the sensitivity), the deck over the exhaust, the fan's swirl
airflow.bench_proof: the thermometer, as the J501's own criterion: the box at 40 W (a 40 W nvpmodel under load) with the adapter on and the turret parked, a thermocouple in the collar 10 mm over the grille and one in the room 0.5 m away at the same height, logged for 30 min: the intake within 3 K of the room, and the module's temperatures from tegrastats no worse than for the same 30 min without the adapter (task N17)
airflow.note: hand estimate on the J501 0.9-g48r fan and its CFD's operating point (not converged: rerun this build when it settles); the mouth is as wide as the deck's front legs allow

intake_seal.note: the J501 roof is solid on top from the grille's openings out to its first open hex cell (the grille's rim, the skirt's top, a band of cells closed by a 1.2 mm skin: its cad/build.py); the foam ring lies in the middle of that band, so no exhaust cell opens inside it. The open cells under the shroud's floor vent through the 1 mm under it

design_gates.toolkit: cadagent.gates (connectivity, containment, relation table, fasteners, motion)

exhaust.fan_blows: up (exhaust through the lid grille; J501 thermal.fan.note)

plume.how: the J501 fan blows up into the shroud, whose duct throws the plume forward out of the deck's mouth, where it rises: the box ahead of the mouth is kept clear of the turret at every pan of the grid, level and fully depressed

exhaust.note: the J501 exhaust leaves the deck's front mouth (158.0 mm wide, z 100.0-137.0), 12.0 mm above the J501's highest intake vent, with the front corners walled; the plinth breathes 94.5 mm behind the mouth; no part of the turret comes within 12.5 mm of the plume's keep-out ahead of the mouth at any pan or tilt. To prove on the bench: the J501's intake and the J4012's within 3 K of the room with both at full load (bench_proof)

shroud_fit.how: the BRepExtrema distance between the intake shroud and each leg (the deck cut round it, under the deck plate) and anything of the deck below its plate at each TM insert (none: the inserts are wholly in the 8 mm deck)

tipping.note: J501: 368 g printed (its slice report) + 1.0 kg Orin, carrier and cooler (est); a sideways push at the tilt axis that lifts the box off its narrow edge

overspeed.note: the flywheel rail, trimmed per turret (11.31 V nominal: the faster X2216 turns 15722 rpm with no load), is the ceiling (D68): at full throttle a ball leaves at about 30 m/s by this page's rough model; the physics' fastest accepted round (22.2-22.8 mm, 1.6-2.0 g) with every tolerance: 103.91 fps on Ø38 tyres, docs/turret-physics.md section 4, under the 105 fps ceiling and ASTM F963's 2,500 J/m2; the barrel's two gates trip the safety line on any ball over 105 fps. Eye protection recommended, as Hasbro does for Rival

release.note: a ball that has already dropped still fires up to 102 ms after ARM is released; the phase-short brake (six FETs on the cartridge board, 5-14 ms after the line drops) stops the wheels to 5 % about 80 ms after release (docs/turret-physics.md section 5), where unbraked they would coast 1.3 s

checks.lid_screw: M3 x 40 ISO 4762, tip at z 62 (as the J501's own M3 x 16)
